items.headline: Three Mile Island nuclear plant will reopen to power Microsoft data centers
items.dek: Three Mile Island, the Pennsylvania power plant that was the scene of the worst commercial nuclear accident in American history, will reopen and sell power to Microsoft.

items.caption: NPR article header: headline, dateline Sept 20 2024, byline, and Getty photo of TMI cooling towers (Jeff Fusco/Getty Images)
items.notes: Body (verbatim): 'The agreement will span 20 years, and the plant is expected to reopen in 2028. It will be renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center in honor of Chris Crane...' Restart has since been pulled forward to 2027.

items.slide_topic: Three Mile Island / Crane restart for Microsoft
items.headline: Three Mile Island is reopening and selling its power to Microsoft
items.dek: Three Mile Island, the site of worst nuclear disaster in the United States, is reopening and will exclusively sell the power to Microsoft as the company searches for energy sources to fuel its AI ambitions.
items.author: Jordan Valinsky
items.caption: CNN header: huge headline, byline, AFP/Getty photo of TMI cooling towers venting steam (ad box at right)

items.headline: Constellation seeks FERC help with Crane restart
items.dek: When the former Three Mile Island-1 restarts in 2027 as the Crane Clean Energy Center, it will not face a delay of several years before it can be reconnected to the grid, Constellation CEO Joseph Dominguez said this week.
items.caption: Nuclear Newswire article: headline, aerial photo of TMI before its 2019 shutdown (Constellation), first two paragraphs incl. PJM 2031 grid-connection analysis
items.notes: Verbatim: 'a Reuters report on an analysis from electric grid provider PJM suggesting the plant may not be connected to the grid until 2031.' Dominguez: 'We are working on that with PJM, and we continue to expect to start this unit in 2027.' FERC later granted the waiver (Constellation Q2 2026 release).

items.headline: Incident pauses Palisades fuel loading; plant connected to switchyard
items.dek: An incident involving a fuel assembly has paused the fuel loading process at the Palisades power plant in Covert, Mich., operator Holtec has acknowledged.
items.caption: Text-heavy Nuclear Newswire crop: headline + 4 paragraphs describing the tilted fuel assembly
items.notes: Verbatim: 'Fuel loading began on August 30 as Palisades entered Mode 6... The reactor core consists of 204 fuel assemblies'; 'one previously used fuel assembly tilted from its upright position after it had been placed in the vessel.' Switchyard reconnected Sept 11, 2026.

items.headline: Nuclear regulators probe fuel assembly installation mishap at Palisades
items.dek: "There has been no radiological release and no workers or the public have been affected," an NRC spokeswoman said of the incident.
items.author: Keith Matheny
items.caption: Headline-only crop (byline row omitted because author photo failed to load)
items.notes: Edwin Lyman (Union of Concerned Scientists), verbatim: 'I suspect that the rush to do things quickly is leading to mistakes - and you don't like to have too many mistakes when you're talking about a nuclear power plant.' Freep: 'Neither ... Holtec, nor NRC officials released information to the public about the incident for weeks.'

items.headline: Palisades restart delayed
items.dek: The delay follows a fuel-loading incident involving a partially used radioactive fuel assembly.
items.caption: Headline + subhead + date strip
items.notes: NEI calls Palisades an 800 MWe PWR and says the restart is 'delayed indefinitely'. Holtec: 'Progression to subsequent operating modes remains subject to satisfactory resolution of the affected fuel assembly, completion of required testing and modifications, and applicable NRC approvals.'

items.headline: Federal regulators investigating tilted fuel assembly at Michigan nuclear plant
items.dek: Engineers are working on a plan to retrieve the tilted fuel assembly and return it to the spent-fuel pool.
items.caption: MLive header (Oct 3, 2026) + large reactor-vessel photo
items.notes: Most recent status found (Oct 3, 2026). Holtec's Nick Culp: 'Fuel loading remains paused while the affected assembly is addressed. Once that work is complete, fuel loading will resume.' Holtec submitted its retrieval plan to the NRC 'this week'. 204 assemblies: 68 new + 136 partially used; each 12 ft long with 216 rods.

facts.claim: Microsoft signed a 20-year deal to buy power from Three Mile Island Unit 1 - an 835 MW reactor shut in 2019 - so Constellation can restart it as the Crane Clean Energy Center.
facts.source: Microsoft Cloud Blog / Constellation press release

facts.claim: Financial terms of the Microsoft-Constellation 20-year agreement 'weren't disclosed'.
Crane restart was first targeted for 2028; Constellation now says it is 'ahead of schedule' and 'on track to return 835 megawatts ... to the grid in 2027'.
Constellation is spending $1.6 billion to restart the Crane reactor; DOE closed a $1 billion loan for it (announced Nov 18, 2025).

A PJM analysis suggested Crane might not connect to the grid until 2031; FERC then granted Constellation's waiver to move capacity interconnection rights from its Eddystone gas units to Crane, and the NRC approved Crane's fuel licence amendment.
facts.source: ANS Nuclear Newswire; Constellation Q2 2026 results (republished on StockTitan)

facts.claim: NRC issued its final environmental assessment and finding of no significant impact for the Crane restart (Federal Register, Sept 25, 2026); an exemption and three licence amendments are still pending.
A 262-ton transformer, shipped a month from South Korea, reached Three Mile Island on Aug 17, 2026, the first of three new power transformers for the restart.
Palisades (800 MW, shut May 2022) began loading fuel on Aug 30, 2026; a used fuel assembly tilted inside the reactor vessel and loading has been paused since. No restart date has been set.
facts.source: Holtec 'Progress Report on Palisades' March to Startup'; ANS; NEI Magazine

facts.claim: Holtec did not disclose the Aug 30 Palisades incident publicly until a Sept 21 progress report, about three weeks later; NRC says there was 'no radiological release'.
Palisades' restart targets have slipped from end-2025 to early 2026 and now to an open date; Holtec's contract calls for supplying power by March 2027.
Holtec postponed its planned $750M+ IPO in Sept 2026; its CEO blamed uncertainty about US data-center power demand.
Constellation shares fell 'from a high of over $400 last fall to the mid-$260s'; the VanEck Uranium and Nuclear ETF peaked above $160 in January and has lately traded below $110.
Google signed a 25-year deal to buy power from Iowa's Duane Arnold (615 MW, shut 2020); DOE closed a loan of up to $1.9B on Sept 8, 2026; restart targeted no later than Q1 2029.
DOE on Duane Arnold: 'Thanks to President Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge, hyperscalers, not taxpayers, are paying for the new power generation.'
Amazon will take up to 1,920 MW from Talen's Susquehanna nuclear plant through 2042, reaching full volume no later than 2032, alongside a $20B Pennsylvania data-center investment.

Amazon invested in X-energy (Oct 2024); its first project, with Energy Northwest in Washington, is four Xe-100 reactors (320 MW, expandable to 960 MW). The construction permit application is expected to be filed in the first half of 2027.
Google's Kairos deal covers up to 500 MW from six or seven small reactors, the first by 2030 and the rest by 2035; ground was broken on the 50 MW Hermes 2 in Oak Ridge on April 17, 2026.

Meta announced nuclear deals for up to 6.6 GW by 2035: more than 2.1 GW from two Vistra plants in Ohio plus 433 MW of uprates across three Vistra plants, up to eight TerraPower Natrium units (2.8 GW), and an Oklo campus of up to 1.2 GW in Ohio, to power its Prometheus supercluster.

Meta's first nuclear deal was a 20-year PPA for all 1,121 MW of Constellation's Clinton plant from June 2027, which keeps the plant running after Illinois' subsidy ends and adds 30 MW through uprates.
Amazon signed a 20-year, 690 MW PPA for Calvert Cliffs that includes a 190 MW uprate (online 2030-2032) and more than $3B of investment.
Google's first nuclear PPA outside the US is a 22-year deal for 50% of Finland's Loviisa plant over 2030-2049.
Constellation signed another 920 MW of 15-20 year nuclear PPAs in Q2 2026, including a 176 MW Walmart deal that enables a 30 MW uprate at Dresden.
